nodes.description: address public admin: privileged address controlling the timelock in the original design.
address public pendingAdmin: address nominated to become admin after acceptAdmin().
uint public delay: minimum delay enforced between queue and execution of a transaction.
bool public admin_initialized: one-time bootstrap flag allowing the first setPendingAdmin() by admin.
mapping(bytes32 => bool) queuedTransactions: records whether a transaction hash has been queued and not yet executed or cancelled.
uint public constant GRACE_PERIOD = 14 days: window after eta during which a queued transaction remains executable.
uint public constant MINIMUM_DELAY = 1 days: lower bound enforced on the delay.
uint public constant MAXIMUM_DELAY = 30 days: upper bound enforced on the delay.
constructor(address admin_, uint delay_) initializes admin and delay after bounds checks on delay_.
function() external payable: fallback that accepts plain ether transfers to the timelock.
setDelay(uint delay_) public: self-governed update of the delay; requires msg.sender == address(this).
acceptAdmin() public: pendingAdmin claims the admin role and resets pendingAdmin.
setPendingAdmin(address pendingAdmin_) public: nominates a new admin; self-call normally, admin once during bootstrap.
queueTransaction(...) public returns (bytes32): admin-only, hashes and marks a transaction as queued with a timestamp-based eta check.
cancelTransaction(...) public: admin-only, hashes and clears a queued transaction.
executeTransaction(...) public payable returns (bytes memory): admin-only execution of a queued transaction via low-level external call with value.
getBlockTimestamp() internal view returns (uint): returns block.timestamp, isolating time dependence.
msg.sender: caller identity used for all access-control checks in the timelock.
block.timestamp: miner-influenceable time source used for eta, delay and grace-period checks.
target.call.value(value)(callData): low-level external call forwarding arbitrary calldata and ether to an arbitrary target.
Writes to queuedTransactions[txHash]: marking transactions as queued/executed/cancelled, the central execution-state mutation.
Transition of the privileged admin role (admin = msg.sender / admin = admin_).
Constructor parameter delay_: initial governance delay, bounded by MINIMUM_DELAY and MAXIMUM_DELAY.
Constructor parameter admin_: initial privileged address stored into admin.
setDelay parameter delay_: new delay value, bounded and applied to delay.
setPendingAdmin parameter pendingAdmin_: address nominated as the next admin.
target: destination address of the queued/executed transaction, fully attacker-controlled by admin.
value: ether amount forwarded with the low-level call.
signature: function signature string used to build callData when non-empty.
data: raw calldata appended after the encoded selector (or used directly if signature is empty).
eta: earliest execution timestamp, compared against block time, delay and grace period.
bytes32 txHash: keccak256(abi.encode(target, value, signature, data, eta)) used as the queue key.
bytes callData: encoded payload passed to the external call.
bytes returnData: raw return data of the external call, forwarded to the caller.
bool success: result flag of the low-level call, asserted with require.

edges.reason: Constructor parameter delay_ is validated against MINIMUM_DELAY/MAXIMUM_DELAY and stored into delay.
Constructor parameter admin_ becomes the initial privileged admin address.
MINIMUM_DELAY bounds the initial delay value in the constructor.
MAXIMUM_DELAY bounds the initial delay value in the constructor.
constructor writes delay_ into the delay state variable.
constructor writes admin_ into the admin state variable.
constructor sets admin_initialized to false, enabling the bootstrap path.
setDelay requires msg.sender == address(this), so the caller identity gates the delay update.
setDelay parameter delay_ is checked and written into the delay state variable.
MINIMUM_DELAY lower-bounds the new delay in setDelay.
MAXIMUM_DELAY upper-bounds the new delay in setDelay.
setDelay mutates the delay state variable.
acceptAdmin requires msg.sender == pendingAdmin before granting the admin role.
pendingAdmin state variable is compared against msg.sender to authorize the admin handover.
acceptAdmin performs the privileged admin role transition.
The admin role transition writes the stored admin state variable.
acceptAdmin resets pendingAdmin to address(0) after the handover.
setPendingAdmin authorizes either address(this) or the bootstrap admin based on msg.sender.
setPendingAdmin stores its parameter into pendingAdmin.
setPendingAdmin mutates the pendingAdmin state variable.
admin_initialized selects between the one-time bootstrap authorization and the strict self-call authorization.
queueTransaction requires msg.sender == admin before a transaction can be queued.
target is hashed into txHash and is fully controlled by the privileged caller.
value is hashed into txHash for the queued transaction.
signature is hashed into txHash for the queued transaction.
data is hashed into txHash for the queued transaction.
eta is hashed into txHash and validated against block time plus delay.
getBlockTimestamp().add(delay) gates the eta of the queued transaction.
block.timestamp is read by getBlockTimestamp(), making all timing checks miner-influenceable.
queueTransaction enforces eta >= current time + delay using getBlockTimestamp().
queueTransaction derives the local txHash key from the transaction parameters.
txHash is used as the key when writing the execution-state mapping.
queueTransaction writes queuedTransactions[txHash] = true.
The queued/executed flag is stored in the queuedTransactions mapping.
cancelTransaction requires msg.sender == admin before clearing a queued transaction.
target participates in recomputing txHash for cancellation.
eta participates in recomputing txHash for cancellation.
cancelTransaction recomputes the txHash key from its parameters.
cancelTransaction writes queuedTransactions[txHash] = false.
executeTransaction requires msg.sender == admin before performing the privileged call.
executeTransaction requires queuedTransactions[txHash] to be true before executing.
Execution timing is validated against current block time via getBlockTimestamp().
eta.add(GRACE_PERIOD) bounds how long a queued transaction stays executable.
target is the destination of the privileged external call.
value is the ether amount forwarded to the external call.
signature determines whether callData is built from the selector plus data.
data is the payload appended after the selector or used raw when signature is empty.
eta is re-hashed and compared against current time and grace period.
executeTransaction assembles callData from signature and data.
Execution-state is cleared (queuedTransactions[txHash] = false) before the external call.
executeTransaction performs a low-level external call forwarding arbitrary calldata and value to target.
callData is the payload supplied to the external call.
returnData captures the raw return values of the external call.
success captures the boolean result of the external call and is checked with require.
The arbitrary target can re-enter the timelock during the low-level call, although execution state is cleared before the call (checks-effects-interactions).
The success flag of the external call is asserted inside executeTransaction.
returnData is returned to the caller of executeTransaction.

normalization_plan.reason: Constructor parameter delay_ only participates in the constructor, so it folds into the constructor function node.
Constructor parameter admin_ only feeds the constructor assignment and folds into the constructor function node.
setDelay parameter delay_ is local to setDelay and folds into that function node.
setPendingAdmin parameter pendingAdmin_ is local to setPendingAdmin and folds into that function node.
target is first consumed by queueTransaction's hashing and delay check, so it normalizes into queueTransaction.
value flows with target into the queue hash and normalizes into queueTransaction.
signature flows with target into the queue hash and normalizes into queueTransaction.
data flows with target into the queue hash and normalizes into queueTransaction.
eta is validated against block time and delay inside queueTransaction, so it normalizes there.
txHash is produced by queueTransaction and only reuses the function parameters, so it folds into that function.
callData is built and consumed entirely inside executeTransaction.
returnData is produced by the call inside executeTransaction and returned to its caller.
success is a temporary flag checked immediately inside executeTransaction.
